title: Your first tank in a few steps
intro: Ready to get started? This short route covers the essentials. The other chapters explain each feature in more detail.
steps: Sign in and create your first tank with a name, water type and size.
Add animals and plants from the catalogs. Deliberately choose any relevant forms or L-numbers.
Open “New measurement”, choose your test methods and save your first readings.
Record the next care task in the log. Then set a suitable measurement cycle.
Open your profile for language, appearance and test usage. For offline use, first wait for the initial online synchronization to finish.

features.title: Tank
features.text: All records belonging to one tank are kept together here.

features.title: Readings and log
features.text: Readings record values; the log records completed work.

features.title: Add more later
features.text: You can use photos, sharing, AI and Social later as needed.

title: Sign in and get started
intro: You need the address of your aquarium app and a user account. You can read this guide without signing in.
caption: The sign-in page. The server operator chooses which sign-in methods are available.
steps: Open your app address in a browser. Sign in with your username or email address and password.
No account yet? Choose “Register” if registration is enabled. Enter the required information, then read and accept the terms of use.
Confirm your email address using the link you receive. If no message arrives, check your spam folder and ask the operator to check email delivery.
If you have an invitation, open its link first or enter the invitation code during registration.
If your operator has configured Pocket ID or another OpenID Connect provider, you can use the external sign-in option.

extra.title: Forgot your password?
extra.text: Use the password reset option on the sign-in page and open the link in the email. This requires configured email delivery. Never share your password or confirmation links.

features.title: Sign in
features.text: Your account opens your own tanks and tanks shared with you. Use the same account on each visit.

features.title: Register and verify email
features.text: Registration creates an account. Email verification confirms that the address belongs to you.

features.title: Invitation or external sign-in
features.text: An invitation allows registration on restricted servers. Pocket ID is an alternative sign-in method configured by the operator.

title: Your overview
intro: After signing in, you see your aquariums. Click the logo at the top left to return here at any time.
caption: The overview with a fictional example aquarium.
steps: “My aquariums” shows tanks you own. “Shared with me” contains aquariums whose sharing invitations you have accepted.
Open an aquarium by selecting its card. You will find current readings, warnings, care cycles and the other sections there.
The header links to species, plants, health, Social, notifications and your profile.
Use the language button to switch between German and English. The theme button selects a light, dark or system theme.

When online, the app synchronizes data with the server automatically. The local data timestamp and “Synchronize now” appear only offline. They disappear when the server is reachable again. Pending changes and errors remain visible for review.

extra.title: Why do some sections appear only when scrolling?
extra.text: Charts, residents, plants and the logbook load progressively. Scroll to the section you need. If loading fails, you can retry that section.

features.title: Tank cards
features.text: Each card represents a tank. Tap it to open its readings, residents and care records.

features.title: Owned and shared tanks
features.text: You manage your own tanks. A shared tank’s permission determines whether you can only read or also change records.

features.title: Language and appearance
features.text: The header lets you switch between German and English and between light, dark and system appearance.

title: Create or edit an aquarium
intro: An aquarium keeps measurements, animals, plants, photos and care activities together.
caption: The form for a new aquarium.
steps: Choose “+ New aquarium” in the overview. Enter a name that helps you recognize the tank.
Choose freshwater or saltwater and enter its volume in liters. Add a motto, description and notes if needed.
Check the details and save the aquarium. It will appear in your overview.
To make changes, open the aquarium and choose “Edit”. You can also adjust care cycles using “Configure cycles” in the tank view.
Only delete an aquarium when you no longer need its data. Read the confirmation and export or back up important data first.

extra.title: Water type and residents belong together
extra.text: The water type affects available species, plants and assessments. Before changing it, check whether the existing residents are suitable.

features.title: Name, water type and size
features.text: These fields describe your tank. Water type and size help put readings and animal care into context.

features.title: Description and cover image
features.text: A motto, text and photo make multiple tanks easier to distinguish. They do not replace readings or care records.

features.title: Edit and delete
features.text: Editing corrects tank details. Deleting removes the tank and its associated records and requires deliberate confirmation.

title: Remember the next water test
intro: The measurement cycle shows when you plan to check the water again. It does not take readings automatically.
caption: The measurement cycle shows its status and next due date in the tank.
steps: Open the tank and choose “Configure cycles” beside the measurement cycle.
Choose an interval in days or weeks. Select a weekday where offered. An interval of zero disables the cycle.
Enable an email reminder if needed, then save. This requires a verified address and working email delivery.
Read the next due date on the cycle card. “Measure now” opens the usual measurement form.
Save a test you actually performed. Check the updated due date and change the cycle if your routine changes.

features.title: Interval
features.text: This sets how often you want to test, for example every seven days.

features.title: Due or overdue
features.text: The status compares the planned date with the current time.

features.title: Plan doses separately
features.text: Fertilizers have their own plans in the fertilizer area. A measurement cycle is not a dosing plan.

title: Measure and save water parameters
intro: You can record individual readings or a complete set. Empty fields are not saved as measurements.
caption: A pH conflict with an individual value choice; independent readings remain in the test.
steps: Open your aquarium and choose “New measurement” or “Measure now”. Check the measurement time.
Open “Customize water tests” and select the tests you actually use. You can combine methods from different manufacturers.
“Apply suite” replaces your selection with that test suite. “Add suite” extends it; one method remains selected for each water parameter.
Follow the instructions supplied with your water test. Start the timer next to a parameter if needed. Several timers can run at the same time.
Enter the result you read. A decimal comma is accepted. The color indicator helps you interpret the value.

Choose “Pause test” to return to the overview and measure at the next aquarium. Expand “Open tests” at the bottom right and select an aquarium to resume. Starting another test for the same aquarium asks whether you want to return to its open test.

To switch devices, wait for pending changes to sync while connected and sign in with the same account on the other device. Open “Open tests” there. Offline you can continue previously downloaded drafts; let local saving finish before closing the app.

If differing entries are reported, expand the local changes and choose “This device” or “Other device” for each affected field. Select “Apply selected values”; equal values and independent additions need no decision.
Add a note if needed and choose “Save measurement”. The reading appears in the aquarium history and logbook.

extra.title: Timers and notifications
extra.text: Choose “Enable” to allow browser notifications. Sound, vibration and keeping the screen awake depend on your device. Keep the app visible for important reaction times; phones may suspend background processes. Expired timers offer “Stop timer” and “Open test”. Stopping removes only the timer and preserves entered values. Opening resumes the corresponding test and automatically pauses another open test. If the matching test is already open, the view stays unchanged. System notifications offer these actions where supported by the browser; clicking the notification also opens the test in its original tab.

extra.title: Changing methods during a measurement
extra.text: Changing the test method may discard a running timer and an unsaved value for that parameter. Choose the method before starting the test whenever possible.

extra.title: Parameter and unit
extra.text: A parameter is a measured quantity, such as temperature or pH. Its unit appears beside the field, for example °C or mg/l. Use the unit and result of your actual test; different units are not interchangeable without conversion.

extra.title: Offline and simultaneous editing
extra.text: Changes remain in the account-specific queue even offline. Devices sync on reconnect, when returning to the app and normally every 30 seconds while visible. If one device adds pH and another adds nitrate, both readings are merged automatically. Equal numbers also match with decimal commas, decimal points or extra trailing zeroes. The starting point distinguishes unchanged entries from intentional corrections and clearing a field. Only conflicting entries require a choice for each affected field: “This device” or “Other device”. Make each choice and select “Apply selected values”; other additions are preserved. Simultaneous changes to notes, measurement times, methods and timers are also protected from silent overwrites. Closed or replaced test sessions are never restored automatically. Read-only shares do not expose drafts; users with write access each have their own tests. Timers keep their original deadlines. Mobile background notifications depend on the device.

features.title: Choose a test method
features.text: Choose the test you actually use. The selection determines the timers offered and which test inventory receives the usage.

features.title: Start a timer
features.text: A timer reminds you of a test’s reaction time. It does not perform the test or enter its result.

features.title: Save readings and time
features.text: Only completed values are saved. An earlier timestamp is useful when recording a test you performed before opening the app.

features.title: Pause tests for each aquarium
features.text: Values, test selection, measurement time with its original time zone, notes and timer deadlines are stored locally for each account and aquarium and synced with your other devices when connected. The expandable “Open tests” button lists these drafts. “Pause test” returns to the overview; reloading and closing preserve drafts already saved locally. Signing out hides them; signing in again with the same account restores them. “Save measurement” creates the measurement and closes its draft together; “Discard test” removes the draft after confirmation on all devices once synced.

title: Set up and calibrate a YINMIK meter
intro: Electronic meters need appropriate preparation. The wizard guides you through the selected model; you perform every action on the actual meter yourself.
caption: Demo: Calibration from a paused test. The test resumes automatically after the last confirmed step.

features.title: Model-specific steps
features.text: Seven meter families are available as test suites. The wizard shows procedures for the selected parameters and identifies button sequences missing from public sources.

features.title: Before each use
features.text: The short procedure covers samples, stable readings, units and cleaning. A completed checklist is not a calibration certificate. In an active test, Calibrate meter saves locally, pauses the form and reopens it afterwards.

features.title: Read offline
features.text: After a complete online sync, guides and the wizard are available offline. Manufacturer links require internet. Readings are entered manually.

steps: Open test selection in your profile or under New measurement. Choose the exact YINMIK model and add individual parameters or the entire suite.
The wizard opens. Compare model, buttons and probe with the supplied manual; stop if they differ. Prepare the specified standards and clean containers.
Perform each step on the meter. Confirm it only after a successful check; use the exact model manual for missing button instructions. Back lets you review previous steps.
After calibration, check a fresh portion of the standard. Wait for stable sample readings and observe entry units; for example, 3.5% salinity equals 35 ppt.

Close the wizard and enter readings. In an active test, choose Calibrate meter directly on a measurement card. The test is saved locally and paused. The last confirmed step automatically reopens it; cancelling also returns without losing readings, notes or running timers. The meter button in test selection also opens the wizard.

extra.title: Matching standards and probe
extra.text: Do not interchange pH buffer families. S-200 uses 3.5% salinity standard, not EC standard. Do not enter oxygen saturation percentages as mg/l. Conditioning, assembly, electrolyte, polarization time and storage depend on your exact probe.

extra.title: No remote device control
extra.text: The app does not connect through Bluetooth or verify hardware. Completing the wizard does not calibrate other meters. If readings are unstable or the check measurement fails, stop measuring and follow the device manual for troubleshooting.

title: Understand charts, tables and warnings
intro: Current readings appear near the top of the aquarium. The history shows how your water changes over time.
caption: Measurement history with a date-range selector and an example chart.
steps: Scroll to “History” in the aquarium. Choose a range such as seven days, three months, one year or all time.
For your own date range, choose “Custom” and set the start and end dates.
Compare the curve with the target range and marked critical limits. A single reading does not explain what caused a deviation.
The measurement table lists dates, values and notes. More rows load when needed.
Warnings appear in the aquarium and under “Notifications”. Check the reading and the conditions in your tank before acknowledging a warning.
With sufficient permission, you can delete an incorrectly recorded measurement. This does not restore the water test already consumed.

extra.title: Colors provide guidance
extra.text: Assessments depend on water type, stocking profiles and available thresholds. They do not replace a professional assessment of your aquarium.

features.title: Latest readings
features.text: The tank shows the latest available reading for each parameter. Check its date: an old reading may not describe today’s conditions.

features.title: Charts and target ranges
features.text: The line shows changes over time. Highlighted ranges help compare readings with stored limits; they do not explain the cause of a deviation.

features.title: Table and warnings
features.text: The table shows individual readings and notes. A warning highlights a deviation; acknowledging it only records that you have seen it.

title: Record care in the logbook
intro: Use the logbook to record work on your tank. Measurements appear there too.
caption: A new logbook entry for a water change.
steps: Choose “New logbook entry” in the aquarium. Set the time and type of work.
For water changes, enter the percentage of water replaced. Describe other work in the appropriate fields.
You can document water changes, filter maintenance, plant trimming, new plants, cleaning, fertilization, feeding and other activities.
Save the entry. In “Aquarium logbook & activities”, filter by activity type or load older entries.
You can edit or delete care entries in your own aquariums or tanks shared with the appropriate permission.

extra.title: Set up reminders
extra.text: Use “Configure cycles” to set measurement and fertilization intervals, such as every seven days or on a specific weekday. The app shows due tasks. Email reminders require enabled reminders and configured email delivery.

features.title: Record care work
features.text: A log entry records work such as filter care, feeding or pruning. This helps explain later changes.

features.title: Water change percentage
features.text: The percentage describes how much water you replaced. In a 100-litre tank, 30 percent is about 30 litres.

features.title: Filter and correct activities
features.text: The combined timeline distinguishes care work from readings. With write permission, you can edit or delete incorrect care entries.

title: Manage fertilizers and dosing plans
intro: The app records fertilization and reminds you of planned work. It does not control a physical dosing pump.
caption: The fertilizer section with an example manual fertilizer.
steps: Scroll to “Fertilizers” in the aquarium. Choose “+ Manual fertilizer” or “+ Dosing pump”.
Enter a clear name, the fertilizer, the amount in milliliters and the interval. Fill in the available time and reminder options.
For a manual fertilizer, confirm a dose you have actually administered using the provided button. This creates a logbook entry.
For automatic pump schedules, the app records due doses according to the plan. Check your physical pump independently.
Edit or pause a plan when your fertilization changes. Removing a plan leaves existing logbook entries intact.

features.title: Manual fertilizer
features.text: The plan reminds you when to dose. Confirm only after adding the fertilizer; confirmation creates the corresponding log entry.

features.title: Dosing pump plan
features.text: An automatic plan records scheduled doses. The app does not operate or monitor a physical pump.

features.title: Amount, interval and pause
features.text: Millilitres specify the dose and the interval specifies how often it occurs. Pausing stops future plan actions without deleting the history.

title: Photos and gallery
intro: Gallery photos belong to your aquarium. They are not automatically published in the public Social feed.
caption: The demo aquarium gallery with an explicitly artificial example illustration.
steps: Choose “+ Upload photo” in the aquarium. PNG, JPG, WebP and GIF are supported up to the displayed five-megabyte limit.
Choose your own image and add a caption. You can set it as the aquarium’s cover photo.
Open a gallery image to view it at full size. You can change captions and the cover photo later.
With sufficient permission, you can delete images you no longer need.
Upload a resident portrait in the residents section. Change your own avatar in your profile.

features.title: Gallery and cover image
features.text: The gallery collects photos for a tank. A cover image helps you recognize that tank.

features.title: Resident photo and avatar
features.text: A resident photo belongs to an animal or group. Your avatar belongs to your user profile. Each has its own upload field.

features.title: Private or published
features.text: A gallery photo does not automatically become a public post. For Social, deliberately create a separate post and choose its visibility.

title: Import and export measurement data
intro: CSV is a simple table format. Use it to transfer data or analyze it in a spreadsheet.
caption: CSV import with a preview and column mapping.
steps: Choose “CSV export” in the aquarium to download measurements. The semicolon option works well with Excel; it creates a CSV file, not an XLSX file.
Choose “CSV import” to bring in existing measurements. Upload a file or use the provided text field.
Check the delimiter and whether the first row contains column headers.
Map each required column to a field such as date, time, pH or note. Ignore columns you do not need.
Review the preview before starting the import. Read any notices about invalid or skipped rows.
After importing, check the history and table. Imported readings are assessed and may count toward test consumption.

extra.title: Before large imports
extra.text: Keep the original file and back up important existing data first. Intentionally importing the same file again is a new action; synchronization deduplication does not replace checking your import selection.

features.title: Export
features.text: Export downloads readings as a table. It is useful for your own analysis but does not contain all app data such as photos or accounts.

features.title: Map columns
features.text: During import, tell the app which column contains a date, reading or note. The preview shows how it understands the file.

features.title: Check an import
features.text: Check timestamps, units and decimal values before importing. Importing a file again can create additional records.

title: Use the species catalog as a reference
intro: You can look up a species without adding a new resident.
caption: Searching for L144: the parent card names the matching form.
steps: Open “Species catalog” in the header.
Filter by water type and category, or search for a species, cultivar or trade name. Matching forms lead to one shared parent card. “Matching forms” lists their names directly on the card.
Open a result. Read its water requirements, group guidance, minimum tank volume, care information and image credits.
If appropriate, add the species to an aquarium from its details or open the linked health information.

features.title: Search and filter
features.text: Search by name or trade name. Water type and category narrow the list when you do not yet know the exact name.

features.title: Matching forms
features.text: If your search matches a form, the shared card names it. You do not need to look for a separate card.

features.title: Species details
features.text: Details explain water requirements, tank size, social needs and behavior. Check the specific selection before adding it.

title: Animals and compatibility
intro: Add animals through the species catalog whenever possible so their care requirements can be associated with them.
caption: Residents in the tank: name, quantity and actual form remain visible together.
steps: Open “Species catalog” and search for the species. Check its water type, tank volume and group requirements.

Choose “Add to aquarium” from the parent entry. Select a documented form or variety in “Form / subspecies”, or leave it unspecified. Then enter the quantity; individual animals can have names. The Ancistrus card also offers documented L-numbers. “Separate species” and “Undescribed / unidentified species” are not subspecies; check their own parameters in the selection hint.

In the aquarium, you can also add custom residents, change quantities and names, or upload a portrait. “Form / subspecies” identifies the selected form, including individually named animals and offline.
For known species, “Species details” opens their information again. You can also start the diagnosis assistant from a resident.
Read compatibility guidance on group size, tank size, behavior and requirements. Custom entries without a catalog match have less automatic information.
Remove animals that are no longer in the tank so assessments and thresholds reflect the current stock.

extra.title: Browse the species catalog
extra.text: Filter by water type and category or search by name. Viewing an image does not share your aquarium. Sources and image credits are listed in the species details.

features.title: Add from the catalog
features.text: The catalog entry connects a resident to care information and the health area. The selected form receives its own stock entry.

features.title: Group or individual animal
features.text: The quantity represents a group. Individual names let you track animals separately, for example a pleco named “Goldie”.

features.title: Compatibility and custom entries
features.text: Hints compare known requirements. Custom entries may lack catalog information; no warning is not a guarantee of suitable care.

title: Choose cultivated forms, plant cultivars and L-numbers
intro: A shared card can contain several selectable entries. A trade name or L-number is not automatically a scientific subspecies.
caption: L183 is labeled as a separate species and the selection shows its own parameters.
steps: Search the appropriate catalog for a form, for example “Pangolino”, “Gold” or “L183”. The parent card identifies the matching entry.
Open “Add to aquarium”. Choose the tank and then the form. For bristlenose catfish, the field is “Species / L-number / form”.
Read the selection hint. Separate Ancistrus species have their own parameters; the shared card’s base parameters do not apply to every L-number.
Enter the quantity and save. The tank keeps the actual selection visible, including for individually named animals.
If identification is uncertain, do not invent a subspecies. Use the unspecified base entry or a suitable custom entry and clarify the identification.

features.title: Cultivated form or cultivar
features.text: This is a selectively bred appearance, such as a particular color or leaf shape.

features.title: Separate species
features.text: Sharing a selection card does not make a separate species a subspecies of another.

features.title: L-number and synonyms
features.text: L-numbers identify particular loricariid catfish. Several numbers may find the same entry; not every L-number catfish belongs to Ancistrus.

title: Find plants and add them to a tank
intro: The plant catalog helps you find suitable plants and record the stock in your aquarium.
caption: Plants in the aquarium: selected forms such as Pangolino are explicitly identified.
steps: Open “Plants” in the header. Filter by water type or category, or search for a species or cultivar name. Forms appear under a shared parent card; “Matching forms” lists the forms found by your search.
Open a plant and read its placement, lighting, growth and care guidance.

Choose “Add to aquarium”, select a suitable aquarium and, if offered, the specific form in “Form / subspecies”. Enter the quantity and save. The selected form keeps its own stock entry. In the aquarium, “Form / subspecies” also identifies the selected form, including offline.
In the aquarium’s plant section, you can change quantities or remove plants.
To record trimming or planting in your history, add a separate logbook entry for that work.

features.title: Look up plants
features.text: Details help with lighting, placement, growth and care. The catalog also includes labeled moss and algae entries.

features.title: Choose a cultivar
features.text: Cultivars such as Pangolino and Pinto appear under their shared card. Select one when adding; it remains identifiable in the tank.

features.title: Change total quantity
features.text: The quantity is the total stock of that plant in the tank. Changing three to five means five in total, not eight.

title: Diseases, diagnosis and treatments
intro: The health section provides reference information and a question-based assistant. It cannot provide a definitive veterinary diagnosis.
caption: The health catalog with search and filters.
steps: Open “Health”. Filter the disease catalog by water type, resident type or search term.
Open an entry and read its symptoms, causes, guidance, sources and associated treatments.
To use the diagnosis assistant, select its tab or launch it from an aquarium or resident.
Choose the aquarium and resident. Answer the questions as accurately as possible. Relevant current water readings may inform the assessment.
Read the list of possible conditions, the information it uses and the limits of the result. Seek professional help if you are unsure or symptoms are serious.
Under “Medications & supplies”, search for products and read their details, warnings, sources and legal information.

extra.title: Offline diagnosis and AI are separate
extra.text: Once the required catalogs and aquarium data have been downloaded, local diagnosis can work without a connection. An optional follow-up AI chat requires a connection and configured AI access.

extra.title: Do not medicate based only on a list of matches
extra.text: Read the entry’s guidance, product instructions and professional advice. An association shown in the catalog is not an individual treatment recommendation.

features.title: Disease catalog
features.text: It explains typical signs, possible causes and further information. Search and filters help you find relevant entries.

features.title: Diagnosis assistant
features.text: The assistant asks questions and ranks possible causes. It does not examine the animal and cannot replace a professional diagnosis.

features.title: Look up treatments
features.text: Linked treatments and supplies provide further information. A match is not a recommendation to medicate immediately.

title: Start the diagnosis assistant
intro: First choose the affected animal or group. This is preselected if you start from the residents section.
caption: The diagnosis assistant with aquarium and resident selection.
steps: Check the aquarium and resident selection.
Start the questionnaire and answer each question in turn.
Review the result together with water readings, husbandry conditions and animal behavior. You can restart the assistant with updated information.

features.title: Tank and resident
features.text: The selection determines which animal and water type your answers refer to. Individual names and stored forms help identify it.

features.title: Yes, no or unknown
features.text: Answer only what you have observed. “Unknown” is better than a guess and is considered in the result.

features.title: Interpret the result
features.text: The list provides guidance. Consider recent readings, natural coloration, care conditions and behavior together.

title: Look up medications and supplies
intro: This catalog supplements disease details. It does not replace professional advice.
caption: Medications and supplies with search and filters.
steps: Open “Health”, then “Medications & supplies”.
Search by name or narrow down the list using the available filters.
Open the medication details. Pay particular attention to warnings, restrictions, sources and legal information.
Consult a knowledgeable professional or veterinarian where needed; do not apply a treatment based solely on a search result.

features.title: Medication or supply
features.text: This area contains information about treatments and supportive measures. Read the details instead of deciding by product name alone.

features.title: Warnings and other residents
features.text: Consider fish, shrimp, snails and plants. The same treatment can have different suitability for different residents.

features.title: Sources and use
features.text: Sources show the basis of the information. Follow the instructions for the actual product and veterinary advice where appropriate.

title: Set up the optional AI assistant
intro: AI is optional. You can manage your aquariums without your own AI access.
caption: AI settings in the profile. No real access keys are shown.
steps: Open your profile using your username and select the AI tab.
Choose an available provider, such as OpenAI, Google Gemini or Anthropic Claude. Enter your personal API key if the operator does not provide suitable access.
Choose an available model and save the settings. Use the connection test to check the setup.
In an aquarium, open the AI button once usable access is configured. Write a question or choose a quick question.
The app shows its progress while processing a request. If an error occurs, you can edit the question and send it again.
Remove personal keys you no longer need in your profile.

extra.title: What data is sent?
extra.text: An AI request sends your message and relevant aquarium context to the selected provider. Aquarium chats may save a conversation history; a chat after diagnosis is not saved as aquarium chat history when closed. Check the provider’s costs, privacy terms and responses. Never include keys in screenshots or Social posts.

features.title: Provider, model and key
features.text: The provider processes your request and the model answers it. An API key is your personal provider credential and should not appear in screenshots or posts.

features.title: Test the connection
features.text: The test checks the saved credentials. A successful connection does not guarantee the accuracy of later answers.

features.title: Ask about a tank
features.text: Quick questions or your own text start a request using the offered tank context. This needs internet and may incur provider charges.

title: Profile, appearance and account security
intro: Click your username in the header. Tabs separate personal details, appearance, AI, tests and invitations where available.
caption: The fictional demo account’s profile.
steps: Edit the available personal details, bio and avatar in your profile. Save your changes.
In the appearance section, choose your language, theme and default chart date range. You can also check supported notifications there.
With a local account, you can change your password. Changing your email address may require confirmation again.
If your operator has configured OpenID Connect, use the relevant section to link or unlink that sign-in method.
If user invitations are enabled, create codes or email invitations and view their status in the invitations tab.
Use “Sign out” in the header when finished, especially on shared devices.

extra.title: Delete your account
extra.text: Request account deletion in your profile, then confirm using the time-limited email link. This also removes associated aquariums you own and your Social content. Back up important data and synchronize pending changes first. Protected administrator accounts may have deletion restrictions.

features.title: Personal details
features.text: Your name, bio and avatar describe your account. Your username also helps other users find you for sharing.

features.title: Appearance and chart period
features.text: Choose the language, design and initial chart period here. You can still change the period in an individual chart.

features.title: Timer notifications
features.text: Browser permission allows supported timer notifications. Sound settings, background rules and power saving can affect delivery.

title: Forgotten password or sign-in changes
intro: This chapter helps you regain account access. These actions require a reachable server.
caption: Password recovery starts on the sign-in page.
steps: Choose “Forgot password?” on the sign-in page and enter your username or email address.
Open the email and follow its link. Enter and repeat a new password, then sign in with it.
If no email arrives, check spam and the address. Ask the operator if delivery is broken; for privacy, the message may not reveal whether an account exists.
If already signed in, change your password under “Password & sign-in” in your profile. An existing local password is required as well.
For external sign-in, check the OIDC link in your profile. Before unlinking, make sure another working sign-in method exists.

features.title: Reset password
features.text: An email link lets you replace a forgotten local password.

features.title: Verify email
features.text: Verification belongs to your account address. You can request another verification email when needed.

features.title: External sign-in
features.text: Pocket ID or another configured provider manages a separate login; change that password at the provider.

title: Delete your own account
intro: Account deletion is permanent. Save needed data and synchronize pending device actions first.
steps: Open your profile and scroll to “Delete account” in the profile tab. Read the explanation.
For local sign-in, enter the required password and deliberately confirm that you want to delete the account.
Request the confirmation email. Until you complete deletion, the request is not a successful deletion.
Open the email link and confirm deletion on the dedicated page. Follow the success message.
If the email is missing or its link fails, contact the operator. Clearing browser data does not delete your server account.

features.title: Sign out
features.text: Signing out ends the session; the account and its server data remain.

features.title: Delete account
features.text: This is a separate action with confirmation and effects on associated data.

features.title: Save first
features.text: Export readings you need or ask the operator about a suitable backup.

title: Select water tests and manage consumption
intro: Test selection defines how you measure. Consumption tracking helps you plan refills.
caption: Test selection and consumption in the profile.
steps: Open the water tests tab in your profile. Select the methods you use and save them.
In the consumption section, select the correct test suite and, where applicable, the variant or refill size.
Enter how much of your current bottle you have already used. Previous measurement history is not fully counted retroactively.
New saved readings increase the corresponding consumption. Empty values do not count. Deleting a measurement does not restore used reagent.
When adding a refill, reset that test’s counter. Adjust its capacity if it differs from the default.
Enable refill reminders if needed. Email notifications require a confirmed address and configured email delivery.

extra.title: Why is the assignment wrong?
extra.text: Check your selected method and suite. A test strip should not count as consumption of a liquid test. The app counts based on the test selection used for the measurement.

features.title: Test selection
features.text: Store your preferred testing methods here. You can select individual methods or entire test suites.

features.title: Variant and capacity
features.text: Choose the package or refill variant. Capacity describes the expected number of tests available from that refill.

features.title: Used and reset
features.text: Enter already used reagent as the starting value. Reset only for a new refill; deleting readings does not refill the bottle.

title: Refills and purchase reminders
intro: Consumption counters help you plan your next purchase in time.
caption: Consumption overview with capacity and refill options for the selected test suite.
steps: Open “Water tests” in your profile and scroll to “Water test usage & refills”.
Select the correct suite and check each test’s variant, total capacity and amount already used.
When starting a new bottle or refill, reset only the corresponding counter.
Enable a purchase reminder if needed. At 75 percent consumption, an email may be queued once per refill if the address and mail delivery are ready.

features.title: Usage level
features.text: The display estimates how many tests remain. It does not replace checking the actual fill level and expiry date.

features.title: Restock reminder
features.text: An enabled email reminder can be queued once per refill after 75 percent usage. It requires a verified address and working email delivery.

features.title: New refill
features.text: Resetting starts usage tracking for that refill again. Other tests and counters stay unchanged.

title: Share an aquarium with other people
intro: Sharing an aquarium is different from publishing a Social post. An aquarium share is granted to a specific user account.
caption: An existing write-access share for the fictional leo_demo account.
steps: Open an aquarium you own and choose “Share aquarium”. Search for the other account’s username or email address.
Choose “Read” if the person should only view the tank. “Write” also lets them maintain supported data.
The invited person accepts the invitation. They can then find the tank under “Shared with me”.
You can review existing shares, change roles or revoke access. Only the owner manages shares.
Invitations and permission changes require a server connection.

extra.title: What do the roles mean?
extra.text: Read access allows viewing data, history, residents and images. Write access additionally allows actions such as measurements, care entries and stocking changes. Only the owner can delete the entire aquarium. Revoking access cannot retroactively erase offline copies already saved on another person’s device.

features.title: Read access
features.text: The person can view the shared tank. This does not give them ownership or administration rights.

features.title: Write access
features.text: The person can also maintain supported tank records. Only the owner manages sharing permissions.

features.title: Invitation and removal
features.text: A new share must be accepted. You can resend pending invitations or remove access later.

title: Share photos, like and comment
intro: Social has its own photo feed. Private gallery and resident photos are not published there automatically.
caption: A server-only demo post with an artificial example illustration.
steps: Open “Social”. Visitors who are not signed in see only public posts; signed-in users also see server-only posts.
To create a post, choose an image and write a caption. Observe the displayed image and text limits.
Check visibility before publishing. New posts are server-only by default. Enable “Show in public feed” only if visitors without an account should see the post.
Use the heart to like a post or remove your like. Open comments to read them or add your own.
“Share” opens your device’s sharing dialog or copies the post link. Internal links still require sign-in.
You can delete your own posts and comments. Administrators can moderate content.

extra.title: Before uploading
extra.text: Use only images you have permission to publish. Check for visible people, addresses, documents or credentials. Social images are resized on the server; animated GIFs are processed as still images.

features.title: Public or server-only
features.text: Public posts can be read without signing in. Server-only posts are intended for users signed in to this server.

features.title: Likes and comments
features.text: A heart records a reaction and a comment adds a message below a post. You need an account to react.

features.title: Share a link and delete
features.text: Sharing passes on a link but does not change visibility. You can remove your own posts and comments; administrators can moderate content.

title: Notifications in one place
intro: “Notifications” collects reactions to your posts and water-parameter warnings from aquariums you can access.
caption: The central notifications area. An empty section means no notifications are currently pending.
steps: Open the notifications button in the header.
Open the associated post or aquarium to review what happened.
Mark Social notifications as read. With sufficient permission, you can acknowledge water-parameter warnings.
Acknowledging records that you have seen the warning. It does not change the reading or fix the cause in your tank.

features.title: Post reactions
features.text: These notifications show likes and comments. Marking them read clears the unread status without deleting the post or comment.

features.title: Water warnings
features.text: A warning takes you to the affected tank. Check the reading and tank conditions before acknowledging it.

features.title: Read does not mean resolved
features.text: Acknowledging a warning does not change a reading. You still need to perform any necessary care or repeat test.

title: Visibility, terms and contact
intro: The page footer links to operator details, privacy information, terms and contact. This public guide can be read without an account.
steps: Use the footer links for legal information, privacy, terms or contact, depending on what you need.
Read the terms before registration. A new version can require signed-in users to consent again.
Confirm only if you agree. If you do not want to continue, you can sign out from the consent dialog.
Distinguish tank shares, server-only Social posts and public posts. Sharing a link does not automatically make private content public.
For account or server questions, contact the listed operator. Do not send passwords, API keys or unsanitized backups.

features.title: Private tank
features.text: Access depends on the account and tank sharing permissions.

features.title: Public post
features.text: The content is intended for visitors without an account as well.

features.title: Guide and contact
features.text: The guide explains usage. The operator helps with access, email and this server’s setup.

title: Work on your phone and without a connection
intro: First open the app online and wait for automatic synchronization of your aquarium data to finish.
caption: Mobile view without a connection and with a demo measurement waiting to upload.
steps: Use your app’s HTTPS address on your phone. An HTTP address on your home network is not sufficient for offline features.
You can add the app to your home screen through the browser menu. Menu names differ between iPhone and Android.
Wait for synchronization on your first online visit. Catalogs and images may take additional time.
Without a connection, view synchronized aquariums and queue supported measurements, care entries and edits locally.

When the server is unavailable, you see the local data timestamp, pending changes and “Synchronize now”. Reconnecting synchronizes automatically and hides the timestamp and button. Keep the app open for this.
Before switching devices or deleting browser data, wait until no pending changes remain.

extra.title: What still needs a connection?
extra.text: New sign-ins, account security, AI, invitations and sharing, Social and administration require a connection. Catalogs are available offline only after downloading. Your operating system may suspend a closed or background app.

extra.title: When two devices change the same data
extra.text: The app shows a conflict. Compare local and server data. “Keep local version” tries to save your version against the new baseline; another conflict is possible. “Discard” removes the local action and, where applicable, dependent actions. Independently recorded entries from different devices remain separate.

extra.title: Local data is not a backup
extra.text: Pending changes exist only on this device and are not included in server backups. Browser data can be deleted. Synchronize regularly. Sign in again after an account change if another tab has changed your session.

features.title: On the home screen
features.text: An installed web app opens like a separate application. Installing it alone does not download all tank data.

features.title: Saved locally
features.text: Local means on this device in the browser you are using. Other devices and server backups receive a change only after successful synchronization.

features.title: Automatic synchronization
features.text: With a reachable server, the open app synchronizes data. Offline, you can see the local data timestamp and try to synchronize manually.

title: Understand pending changes and conflicts
intro: Changes recorded offline wait on this device. For open water tests, the app compares individual entries: additions and equal readings merge automatically. Conflicting changes require your choice.
caption: A pH conflict with an individual value choice; independent readings remain in the test.
steps: Open the list of locally saved entries when synchronization is pending. Check which action is waiting.
Reconnect and keep the app open. Offline, you can use “Synchronize now”.
For a conflict, read the local and server versions. Decide which data is still correct.
For water tests, choose “This device” or “Other device” only for the displayed differing fields and click “Apply selected values”. One-sided additions and equal numbers need no decision.
“Apply local version” retries your change against the new starting point. Another conflict is possible if the record changes again.
“Discard” removes the local action; dependent actions may also be removed. Independent entries stay separate.
Before switching devices or clearing browser data, wait for synchronization to finish. For an error, also check current write permission.

features.title: Pending
features.text: The change is saved locally but has not been confirmed by the server.

features.title: Conflict
features.text: The same data changed since your starting point, so it is not simply overwritten.

features.title: Discard or apply
features.text: You decide what happens to the pending local action. That decision is not a backup.

features.title: Merge individual readings
features.text: The sync compares the starting point, your entry and the other device’s current version. You can decide for each conflicting field while retaining other readings. Changes to different parameters and equal numbers do not trigger unnecessary prompts.

title: Online features when disconnected
intro: Some features need the server, including Social, sharing, account security and AI. If it cannot be reached, a clear offline notice appears.
caption: Actual mobile demo: Social is offline; “Check now” has retried the request and reports that the connection is still unavailable.
steps: Check your Wi-Fi or mobile connection. Even with Wi-Fi connected, the app server may be unreachable.
Tap “Check now”. The app retries the same request. Without a connection, the notice stays open; with a connection, the action continues.
Use “Close” to cancel the request and continue using local aquarium data. Open the feature again later to start a new attempt.
If the connection broke while saving, check whether the action already succeeded before retrying. Otherwise, repeating it could create duplicate changes.

extra.title: No automatic online actions
extra.text: These requests are not stored persistently and are not replayed automatically when reconnecting. Changing the view or signed-in account discards the pending retry. Locally queued aquarium actions still synchronize through their separate offline queue.

features.title: Offline notice
features.text: The notice means the request cannot reach the server. You can continue using local tank data that is already available.

features.title: Check now
features.text: This button retries the paused request. It is different from synchronizing tank actions already saved locally.

features.title: Close
features.text: Closing ends this attempt. It does not store the online request as a task for later.

title: Updates without unexpected reloads
intro: A new app version does not necessarily mean you need to reload the interface.
caption: The real app’s update dialog; an older loaded frontend build was simulated in the demo.
steps: If frontend files change, “New version available” appears. Finish ongoing measurements and save your input.
Wait for the update to be prepared if necessary. “Load now” activates the prepared build and reloads this tab.
Choose “Later” to keep working. Another new build may be offered again.
Changes only to species, plant or health data synchronize separately. They do not require a frontend update dialog.
If an update fails, restore the connection and retry. Other open tabs may still use their previous build.

extra.title: Catalogs are not downloaded on every click
extra.text: Existing offline catalogs are normally checked at most every twelve hours. Failed catalog synchronization can be retried. New data appears in the relevant views after successful synchronization. After the catalog-reading logic changes, the app checks existing catalogs earlier once. Open form selections update after successful synchronization; your selection and input are preserved.

features.title: New interface
features.text: A prepared interface update can be activated with “Load now”. This reloads the tab, so save unfinished input first.

features.title: Continue for now
features.text: “Later” lets you continue in the open version. Once all previous tabs are closed, the browser can activate a waiting update normally.

features.title: New catalog data
features.text: Species, plant and health changes are loaded separately. These data changes do not need an interface update notice.

title: For operators: initial setup
intro: On an empty installation, the setup assistant guides you through the first settings. Afterwards, manage the app in the admin area.
caption: The setup assistant on an isolated, empty demo installation.
steps: Open the new installation and create the first administrator account. Use a reachable email address and your own strong password.
Choose who can register: anyone, invited people only or nobody. You can change this later.
Configure SMTP for email delivery or leave it disabled for now. Without email delivery, confirmation messages, password resets and email reminders will not work reliably.
Configure automatic backups if needed and keep the backup password safe.
Complete setup. For public use, configure the correct public HTTPS address and reverse proxy if applicable.

extra.title: Install or update
extra.text: The repository’s technical documentation describes installation and server configuration. This user guide explains everyday use. Docker commands and server credentials belong with the operator.

features.title: First administrator account
features.text: This account manages the new installation. Regular users do not need administrator access.

features.title: Registration and email
features.text: Registration mode determines who can create an account. Email delivery is needed for confirmations, invitations and reminders.

features.title: Public address and backups
features.text: Mobile and offline use need a suitable HTTPS address. Backups preserve the server state for a later emergency.

title: Manage users and administrator access
intro: Only authorized administrator accounts can see the admin area. Regular users do not need it for aquarium care.
caption: The demo administrator’s user management view.
steps: Open “Admin” and the user management tab. Search by username or email address.
If needed, create an account using the available fields. Give each person their own account.
To correct details, edit the right user. Check the address and email verification status before saving.
Grant administrator access only to people who may manage users and server settings. A tank share is sufficient for working on one tank.
Delete an account only after checking the consequences and confirmation. Save any needed data first.

features.title: Manage users
features.text: You can find or create accounts and change the available account details. Check the affected person before each change.

features.title: Administrator access
features.text: Administrators can manage server-wide settings and users. This is broader than write access to one tank.

features.title: Delete accounts
features.text: Deleting a user can affect associated data. Read the confirmation and save any needed data first.

title: Administration: manage invitations
intro: Registration and invitations control who can create an account on your server.
caption: Registration mode and invitation management.
steps: Open “Admin”, then “Invitations & registration”.
Choose open registration, administrator invitations only, user invitations or closed registration. Check the effect before saving.
Create a code or email invitation and set its expiration and usage limit.
Share invitations only with the intended person and revoke invitations you no longer need.

features.title: Registration mode
features.text: Open allows normal registration. Invitation modes require a valid code; closed prevents new registrations.

features.title: Code or email
features.text: A code can be passed to the intended person. An email invitation sends access through the configured mail server.

features.title: Expiry and usage limit
features.text: These settings limit how long and how often an invitation can be used. Revoking invalidates an invitation you no longer need.

title: Administration: view metrics
intro: This overview summarizes the available usage counts, such as users, aquariums and AI usage.
caption: The metrics area with its additional password prompt.
steps: Open “Admin”, then “Metrics”.
If needed, set up the separate metrics password or use it to unlock the view.
Read the aggregated figures and available breakdowns. These are operational statistics, not assessments of your aquariums.

features.title: Summary counts
features.text: The overview shows aggregate operating figures such as accounts and tanks. It does not rate the quality of animal care.

features.title: AI usage
features.text: Requests and reported token counts provide a usage overview. They do not replace the provider’s billing information. Tokens are small pieces of text counted by an AI provider during processing.

features.title: Additional lock
features.text: The metrics password provides extra protection for this area. It is independent of your normal account password.

title: Email delivery and operator details
intro: These settings affect everyone using your installation.
caption: Email delivery and operator settings in the demo.
steps: Open “Settings” in the admin area. Enter the SMTP server, port, encryption, credentials and sender address supplied by your email provider.
Save and send a test email. Check that it arrives. If it fails, review credentials, encryption, spam folders and server logs.
Check the mail queue when messages are delayed. Not every message is delivered immediately.
Maintain the available operator, contact and legal details for your installation. Public pages are also linked in the footer.
Under “Logs”, search messages and filter by severity. Older entries load progressively; review logs for personal data before sharing them.

features.title: SMTP connection
features.text: SMTP is how the app sends email. The mail provider supplies the host, port, encryption settings and credentials.

features.title: Test email and queue
features.text: A test email checks delivery. The queue shows pending or failed deliveries; it is not an inbox.

features.title: Operator details
features.text: Contact information and legal details apply to the whole installation. Check the public pages after saving changes.

title: Administration: find errors in logs
intro: System logs help you investigate technical problems.
caption: The demo system log with search and filters.
steps: Open “Admin”, then “Logs”.
If needed, choose a severity such as warning or error and enter a search term.
Load older entries if the message you need is not yet visible.
Read each message together with its timestamp and the action performed. Remove personal data and credentials before sharing an excerpt.

features.title: Filter messages
features.text: Severity and search terms help locate relevant events. Warnings and errors can have causes other than incorrect user input.

features.title: Compare timestamps
features.text: Compare the log time with when the problem occurred. This helps connect an error to the relevant action.

features.title: Share or clear logs
features.text: Share only checked excerpts without personal data or credentials. Clearing removes diagnostic information and does not fix the cause.

title: Administration: back up and restore
intro: Backups protect data already saved on the server. Pending offline actions on other devices are not included.
caption: The backup area. No actual restore was performed in the demo.
steps: Open “Backups” in the admin area. Create a manual backup and choose the available image and encryption options.
Download important backups and store them separately from the app server. Back up the server’s shared app encryption key separately as well.
For automatic backups, set the interval, retention and available password and file options.
Before restoring, all users should synchronize pending offline actions. Also create a current backup of the existing server state.
Choose only a trusted backup and read the confirmation. Restoring replaces the server’s data; it does not simply append individual rows.
After restoring, check sign-in, aquariums and images. Missing or incorrect keys and passwords can make encrypted data unreadable.

extra.title: Backups are confidential
extra.text: Backups may contain account, aquarium and image data. Do not share them publicly. Local automatic backups alone do not protect against loss of the entire server.

features.title: Create a backup
features.text: A backup contains the saved server state. Depending on the options, it includes images and encryption; pending device actions are absent until synchronized.

features.title: Automatic backups and retention
features.text: A schedule creates backups regularly. Retention determines which older backups are kept.

features.title: Restore
features.text: Restoring replaces the server data. Keep the password and server encryption key safe and stored separately.

title: When something does not work
intro: These checks often help without deleting any data.
steps: A button is missing: check that you are signed in and own the aquarium or have write access. Some features must be enabled by the operator.
A view does not load: check the connection and use “Retry” in that section. Do not delete browser data while offline actions are pending.
An image or catalog is missing offline: open the app online and wait for synchronization to finish. Not every online feature works offline.
An email is missing: check your spam folder and ask the operator to review SMTP, the queue and logs.
A timer gives no notification: check notification permissions, volume and battery-saving mode. Keep the app visible for important reaction times.
A local action remains pending: read the error or conflict, check your permission and deliberately choose whether to keep or discard the local version.
You need support: note the affected section, action and exact error message. Redact personal information and never disclose passwords or API keys.

extra.title: Share this guide publicly
extra.text: The address ends in /handbuch/en/ and requires no sign-in. All accounts and aquarium data shown are fictional. Screenshots show the real app; depending on language, device, permissions and server configuration, buttons may look different or be unavailable.

features.title: Permission or connection
features.text: Missing permissions and an unreachable server are different problems. Read the message in the affected area first.

features.title: Try again
features.text: Reload a failed section or use “Check now”. Before sending again, check whether the action already arrived.

features.title: Ask for help
features.text: State the action, area and exact error. A sanitized screenshot helps; credentials should never be included.
